section_1.title: The Learning Objective (Prerequisite)
section_1.content: Define the goal of a neural network: minimizing error. We introduce the concept of 'Parameters' (Weights/Biases) as the knobs we turn to improve accuracy.
section_1.example: An archer (the network) trying to hit a bullseye. The arrow's distance from the center represents the error.

section_2.title: Defining Failure: The Cost Function
section_2.content: Explain the Cost Function (Mean Squared Error) mathematically as the difference between the prediction and reality, represented as a 3D 'Error Landscape' visualization.
section_2.example: If the archer is 5 meters off target, the Cost Function calculates the 'penalty' for this distance, creating a topographical map where low valleys are 'good' and high peaks are 'bad'.

section_3.title: The Descent Strategy: Gradient Descent
section_3.content: Introduce Gradient Descent as a navigation tool. We explain the derivative (slope) as a compass pointing toward the steepest descent to reach the valley floor.
section_3.example: A hiker lost in a dense fog (the model) on a mountain range, feeling the ground with their feet to find the steepest downhill path to reach the valley floor.

section_4.title: Dynamics: Learning Rate and Convergence
section_4.content: Discuss the 'Learning Rate' parameter. Explain the risk of steps being too large (overshooting) or too small (infinite time to reach the bottom).
section_4.example: The hiker decides how large a stride to take. Too large, they jump over the valley; too small, they take forever to reach the bottom.

section_5.title: Summary and Synthesis
section_5.content: Summarize the iterative loop: Predict -> Calculate Cost -> Calculate Slope -> Adjust Weights. Emphasize that this cycle is how a machine 'learns'.
section_5.example: Visualizing a robot arm iteratively refining its movement until it successfully catches a ball every single time.
